sourceSemantics.productionMeaning: Every completed current view read clears loading in finally, including silent refresh success, response.error and thrown/rejected errors. Silent start still does not set loading, silent errors still retain the existing view, and response/error writes still require currentness. The unchanged request sequence and project/runtime/mount generation guard prevents stale or unmounted completions from changing state.
sourceSemantics.actualSilentRoute: refreshDirectory invokes refresh({ silent: true }) only when viewRequestedRef is true, alongside the existing directory read, then retains its existing optional models load. No timer, retry, dispatch, error policy or provider integration was changed.

currentnessHelper.meaning: Snapshots retain project path/runtime/generation; render context changes and effect unmount cleanup increment generation, so old completions fail the same guard.

sourceSemantics.case81: An earlier nonsilent refresh leaves loading true; current silent directory refresh installs TEST-current-silent-model and clears loading. The earlier completion returns false, cannot restore loading or replace the current view/error, and loadView is called exactly twice.
sourceSemantics.cases82and83: Response-error and Promise rejection each clear the existing pending loading and keep the exact current error, null diagnostics and null view. Resolving the earlier request returns false and preserves those states, with exactly two view calls. These later checks were unreachable after the old RED loading assertion.
sourceSemantics.case84: A newer third nonsilent request leaves loading true; completing the older silent and original first reads remains inert. Only the current latest completion returns true, clears loading and installs TEST-latest-view; exactly three calls.
sourceSemantics.case85: After unmount, completing silent and first reads leaves the saved state object identical; no view installation or loading change and exactly two calls.
sourceSemantics.coverageLimit: These are finite React/happy-dom state/order assertions with controlled API responses. They are not branch-coverage instrumentation or evidence of real vendor execution.
